title: Compressing Intervention Probes That Characterize Structural Dominance of Marginalized DAGs
banked_reason: Delivered tier=subfield below novelty_target=field: the unrestricted optimum Omega_n remains undetermined for n>=5, and no faithful scoped repair reaches field.
gap_reasons: The note proves the universal n+1 isolation-basis upper bound, but it does not determine the unrestricted optimum Omega_n once the Sperner lower bound diverges for n>=5.

The exact 1+c(n) result applies only to pairwise-latent mDAGs, while the chromatic formula is exact only for canonical shared-bit witnesses; the note's own three-node example shows that arbitrary distributions can require fewer regimes.
The Finner inequality supplies population robustness but no finite-sample calibration or power analysis, limiting the package's immediate operational significance.
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved a universal n+1 fixed-value intervention upper bound, an exact chromatic cost for canonical shared-bit witnesses, an exact Sperner-optimal basis for pairwise-latent mDAGs, and a population Finner certificate.  The field-tier claim collapsed because unrestricted witnesses can be cheaper and the exact unrestricted optimum Omega_n remains open from n=5 onward; resolving that optimum or proving a distribution-independent lower bound remains the substantive next step.
tldr: Can an exponentially large all-pattern one-value probing scheme be compressed without losing exact mDAG structural dominance? The proposal advances a precise positive answer: passive observation plus the \(n\) interventions that fix every vertex except one should characterize \(\mathcal M_{\mathcal F}(H)\subseteq\mathcal M_{\mathcal F}(G)\) exactly by edge-and-face inclusion. Its technical core is an iff criterion saying that a canonical shared bit is compatible precisely when the union of all exposed directed sources is a latent face; this yields a chromatic exact cost for that witness class, a robust Finner certificate, and the Sperner-optimal total \(1+c(n)\) basis for pairwise-latent mDAGs, while leaving unrestricted global optimality for \(n\ge5\) open.
gap: The closest theorem, Ansanelli--Wolfe--Spekkens Theorem 3, needs every one-value target pattern and reconstructs missing-face information from subset-indexed shadows. Existing experiment-selection results optimize pair separation or graph recovery under different assumptions; they do not establish nonparametric mDAG model-set containment for higher-order latent faces.
fill: Prove the source-union compatibility theorem and its OR simulator, derive the universal \(n+1\) basis and observable Finner inequality, solve shared-bit basis optimization through minimal-nonface coloring, and establish the exact Sperner basis for pairwise-latent mDAGs. Explicitly separate these results from the unresolved arbitrary-witness and unrestricted \(n\ge5\) minima.
